subject: Valid days, time in intensities and calibration error

messages.author: 9f58683bb92d4062
messages.subject: Valid days, time in intensities and calibration error
parts:
Hi there, 

Thank you for this great package. I am using it for the first time to analyse ActiGraph GT3X hip-worn data (not worn during sleep) and have a few questions.

1. For several participants I seem to get different valid days in different csv files. For example, for one participant, part2_daysummary provides data for 7 valid days as does part5_daysummary_full (from the QC folder) but part5_daysummary WW (not from the QC folder) provides only 4 valid days. 

Is there a potential reason for discrepancies in valid data from the GGIR outputs?

2. To my understanding, time in MVPA differs between part 2 and part 5 due to when MVPA can happen and differences in overlapping with midnight.

Is this correct?

3. When I compare time spent in intensities between the file summary report (colour shadings) and part5_daysummary_full (from the QC folder) they don't always correspond, i.e., the amount of shading doesn't always correspond with the values for LIPA or MVPA in the csv file.
 
Could there be a reason for this?

4. Lastly, the file for this participant and others have a calibration error of 0.006 or 0.007 despite the fact that the file isn't corrupt nor too short. The QC message reads " re-calibration attempted with all available data, but possibly not good enough: Check calibration error variable to verify this". I have tried to use the auto calibration command but it seems that the collaboration error is too high to be fixed by this.

Any suggestions for how to deal with calibration errors higher than 0.005?

Attached is the R script that I used. 

Really appreciate any feedback received,

Kind regards,
Callum

messages.author: 017566be30afa7f3
messages.subject: Re: [GGIR] Valid days, time in intensities and calibration error
parts:
Hi Callum,

  1. Yes, this is intentional. Each part of GGIR has its own definition of a day and criteria to define a valid day and that is why GGIR has all these parts. To understand this you would have to read the documentation https://wadpac.github.io/GGIR/index.html. In short: part 2 is calendar day oriented (midnight-midnight), part 4 night-oriented defined from noon-noon or 6pm-6pm, part 5 can facilitate wakeup-wakeup next day.
  2. See documentation https://wadpac.github.io/GGIR/articles/chapter12_TimeUseAnalysis.html#seemingly-overlapping-variables-between-ggir-part-2-and-part-5-output
  3. See documentation https://wadpac.github.io/GGIR/articles/GGIRParameters.html?q=visualreport#visualreport The file summary report is known to be inaccurate as it was never intended for quality checking data when I first created it. On a positive note I will replace it in the next release with a visual report that is intended for quality checking data. 
  4. I think 0.005 is not too bad, and in studies I have worked on we typically only excluded recordings with more than 0.01 estimated error. However, my response to Gareth a couple of minutes ago may be of interest to you.

Best,

Vincent
